doc: Two friendly rifle squads 20 m apart are ordered onto the same point 35 m east and clump there (sw-txnj.12, GDD 02 §2.14 Separation and coherency). Separation pushes units of different squads apart to their size-class distance (troopers are medium: 0.6 m), so the two squads interleave instead of stacking. Base: both move. Variants: both attack-move (no enemy in reach, so they walk to the point as a move would), and one squad already standing on the point when the other arrives. The far post is an unarmed, stationary dummy that only keeps player 2 in the battle.

arrive_on_squad.doc: North already holds the point; south moves onto it.

probes.doc: While they arrive, a pair may overlap for a tick: a push is capped at the unit's speed (walk per tick when it stands), so two units stepping onto one slot take two ticks to part (0.32 m at worst here).
Settled, no unit of one squad is closer than 0.6 m (medium) to a unit of the other, on any tick of turn 3 (they arrive late in turn 2).
They end interleaved on the point, not just kept apart: the nearest pair is within 2 m.
Spacing within one squad (separation never pushes a squad's own units); reported only.
